title: Building Your Trading Plan
promise: Everything comes together: pick your style and markets, write your entry, exit and risk rules, run a checklist and review every week.
unlock: Pick a trading style that fits your time, and a short list of markets
Write an entry rule you can follow the same way every time
Set your stop, target, size and loss limits before you buy
Run a yes/no checklist before every trade
Review your plan every week and improve it one change at a time

questions.q: You have a busy job. You can look at the market once a day, after it closes, and want to hold for a few days. Which style fits?
options: Swing trading: days to weeks
Day trading: all closed by the bell
Position trading: months, checked weekly
questions.why: Holding a few days with one look after the close is swing trading. Day trading needs you at the screen while markets are open. Position trades last months.
questions.added: New situation written for the Academy

questions.q: Your rule: buy when a pullback to the rising 50-day closes back above it. Today price touched it but closed below. What now?
options: Buy now: it touched the average
Sell: the trend is over
Wait: no close above it yet
questions.why: A touch is only the trigger. Your rule also needs a close back above the average. Until then, no setup.
questions.work: Trend: yes. Pullback: yes. Close above: not yet. No trade.
questions.added: New situation written for the Academy

chart.label: Price pulls back to the rising 50-day average; today’s candle touches it and closes just below

questions.q: Your account is $20,000 and you risk 1% a trade. You buy at $50 with a stop at $45. How many shares?
options: 400 shares: all you can afford
40 shares
80 shares
questions.why: If the stop is hit you lose about $200, your 1%. 400 shares would lose about $2,000 at the stop: 10% of your account.
questions.added: New situation written for the Academy

chart.label: Entry at $50 with the stop at $45, $5 below

questions.q: Five checks say yes. One says no: your target is only 1.5× the risk. What should you do?
options: Take it: close enough
Skip it and wait for a setup that passes
Move your stop closer to make it 2×
questions.why: One “no” means no trade. Moving the stop closer only fixes the numbers: the stop goes where you’re wrong, not where the math works.
questions.added: New situation written for the Academy

questions.q: Your weekly review shows most losses came from moving your stop. What’s the best change?
options: Change your entry, markets and size too
Fix that one thing, then judge it over 20+ trades
Widen all your stops so they get hit less
questions.why: Fix the one thing the journal shows: keep stops where you set them. Then judge it over 20 trades or more. Wider stops just make each loss bigger.
questions.added: New situation written for the Academy

retry.q: You work night shifts and can check the market only once a week, on your day off. You want to hold for months. Which style fits?
options: Day trading: all closed by the bell
Swing trading: days to weeks
Position trading: months, checked weekly
retry.why: One look a week, holding for months, is position trading. Day trades need hours at the screen; swing trades often need a look every day.
retry.added: New situation written for the Academy (retry set)

retry.q: Your rule: buy when a pullback to the rising 50-day closes back above it. The average is falling. Price rises, touches it and closes above. What now?
options: Buy: it closed above the average
No trade: the average isn’t rising
Buy double to catch the turn
retry.why: Every part of the rule must happen, and it starts with a rising average. This one is falling, so there’s no setup.
retry.work: Trend: no. Pullback: yes. Close above: yes. No trade.
retry.added: New situation written for the Academy (retry set)

retry.q: Your account is $5,000 and you risk 1% a trade. You buy at $20 with a stop at $19. How many shares?
options: 250 shares: all you can afford
50 shares
100 shares
retry.why: If the stop is hit you lose about $50, your 1%. 250 shares would lose about $250 at the stop: 5% of your account.
retry.added: New situation written for the Academy (retry set)

retry.q: Five checks say yes. One says no: you already lost $200 today, your daily limit. What should you do?
options: Take it: the setup is great
Skip it: one “no” means no trade
Take it with half size
retry.why: One “no” means no trade, and a loss limit never bends. Half size still breaks the limit. Tomorrow is a new day.
retry.added: New situation written for the Academy (retry set)

retry.q: You changed your target from 2× to 3× the risk. After 5 trades, 3 lost. What’s the best move?
options: Go back to 2× right away
Keep testing to 20+ trades, changing nothing else
Change your entry rule too
retry.why: 5 trades is mostly luck. Keep everything else the same and judge the one change after 20 trades or more.
retry.added: New situation written for the Academy (retry set)

refresher.title: Lesson 1 · Pick your style and markets
refresher.text: Pick the style that fits the time you really have. Day trading needs hours at the screen while markets are open. Swing trades get a look once a day; position trades about once a week.

refresher.title: Lesson 2 · Your entry rules
refresher.text: Every part of the rule must happen: trend, pullback, then a close back above. A touch alone is not a setup.

refresher.title: Lesson 3 · Your exit and risk rules
refresher.text: Risk 1% a trade: shares = risk ÷ (entry − stop). On $10,000 with a $50 entry and a $48 stop: $100 ÷ $2 = 50 shares.

refresher.title: Lesson 4 · Your pre-trade checklist
refresher.text: Run 5 to 7 yes/no checks before every trade. One “no” means no trade. Don’t squeeze the stop to fix the numbers: the stop goes where you’re wrong.

refresher.title: Lesson 5 · Review and improve
refresher.text: Change one rule at a time and judge it over 20 trades or more. Several changes at once hide what worked.
